summary: Civil/infrastructure design software is a ~USD 2-4 B/yr market growing ~7%/yr (analyst figures disagree by 60%). Serious civil tools cost USD 1.2k-6k per seat per year; Autodesk, Vectorworks, SketchUp and Land F/X are subscription-only, leaving BricsCAD, Carlson, 12d, Bentley (at ~2.5x annual) and Trimble dongles as the last perpetual options - the clearest pricing gap. Open-source tools live on small recurring donations plus a few corporate patrons (Blender: ~EUR 3.1 M income in FY2024 yet a loss), low-priced pro builds (QCAD, Krita store builds, Ardour pay-what-you-want) or a separate services company (Godot/W4); the VC-backed FreeCAD company Ondsel shut down in Dec 2024 (unverified). On stability, Autodesk's own release notes list 10-17 crash/hang fixes per Civil 3D point release through 2026-2027, its knowledge base has a separate FATAL ERROR article per workflow, and references are path strings in DWGs and per-user XML files that break on every move, rename, drive mapping, permission or cloud-cache difference; each mitigation (autosave, .bak, Recovery Manager, Reference Manager, eTransmit, Bind, Desktop Connector) carries documented fine print, and cloud worksharing turns 'file not found' into 'local changes discarded'. Caveat: the shared search budget ran out after 12 searches and page fetches were proxy-blocked, so BricsCAD/Bentley/Vectorworks crash evidence and several funding pages are unverified; Autodesk evidence comes from the official Autodesk help tool and sibling notes.

praise.theme: Perpetual licensing still exists at the low end
praise.detail: BricsCAD, Carlson, 12d and Trimble still sell perpetual seats; surveyors cite '3 seats of Carlson IntelliCAD for the price of a single seat of C3d' and switching to BricsCAD after 20+ years of AutoCAD over the pricing model.

praise.theme: Open-source funding works at modest scale
praise.detail: Blender grew income to ~EUR 3.1 M with small donors reaching 20% of income and strategic corporate patrons from hardware/renderer vendors; the model transfers to CAD (survey-hardware, workstation, GPU vendors as patrons).
CER sends a minidump, recent command history and system info; reports are triaged by severity and number of customers and reporters are notified when fixed. A new app should match this from day one.

praise.theme: Recovery tooling exists and is documented
praise.detail: AutoCAD ships .bak on save, .sv$ autosave, Drawing Recovery Manager, AUDIT/RECOVER/RECOVERALL, and an optional full-time CRC check; the Reference Manager audits missing references across many drawings without opening them.

praise.theme: Relative paths are now the default
praise.detail: AutoCAD's default xref path type is relative (REFPATHTYPE) and eTransmit's 'organized folder structure' converts absolute paths inside the root to relative, so a project folder can be moved as a unit when everything lives inside it.

praise.theme: CADCraft's engine-level crash discipline is a usable base
praise.detail: No panics in production code, catch_unwind around every command and interactive step with the drawing restored, ~40 hostile-input tests, input caps, background autosave with instance lock files and GPU-fault autosave, AUDIT that never guesses at content (sibling inventory).

complaints.theme: Crash volume is structural, not incidental
complaints.detail: Autodesk's own fixed-issue lists carry ~17 crash/hang fixes in Civil 3D 2027.1 alone, ~12 in 2027, ~15 in 2026.1 and ~11 in 2026.2; 2024.3 fixed two cases where alignment data was lost after save and reopen. Forum users report weekly to daily crashes in 2026.

complaints.theme: Crashes on save and open lose work
complaints.detail: Separate KB articles cover fatal errors on save (corrupt AEC objects; remedy is to export everything to LandXML and re-import, or fall back to the .sv$), on save when proxy graphics exhaust memory, on open from corrupt xrefs or back-saved files; a crash mid-save can leave a truncated DWG with no footer.

complaints.theme: Data shortcuts are per-user path files with no locking
complaints.detail: Each shortcut XML stores a path; in ACC/Forma projects member permissions rewrite that path per user ('truncating or expanding the path ... making it unavailable for others'); 2027.1 fixed host drawings mutating shortcut XMLs 'may not cover all cases'; Autodesk docs state there is no locking for concurrent shortcut edits and folder-structure changes may be lost; syncing over WAN can take hours and 'Repair' hangs.

complaints.theme: Xref paths break on move, drive mapping, permissions, cloud cache or VPN
complaints.detail: Relative paths are unavailable across drives or servers and can fail because 'automatic save is too frequent'; unresolved-xref causes include mapped-vs-UNC, drive letters hijacked by USB devices, paths over 256 chars, stopped DNS services; after a server migration opening drawings can freeze, with the advice to unplug the network cable; the Reference Manager bulk-repaths with no undo.

Desktop Connector sync failures leave files 'Modified' and invisible to co-workers; a 'Conflict' gives priority to the cloud copy and local changes go to the Recycle Bin; 'Free Up Space' before sync deletes unsynced work; file locking is unsupported on long paths; the shortcut-sync balloon can appear before upload finishes so clicking it loads stale data.

complaints.theme: DWG bloat and corruption are routine
complaints.detail: Autodesk lists cloud-sync folders, non-Microsoft networks, NAS/SAN, VPN drops, email and third-party DWG writers as corruption sources; cleanup is a ritual (detach xrefs, OVERKILL, -PURGE regapps, reset scale list, WBLOCK into a new file); files stay ~8 MB after deleting everything; RECOVER can itself stall at 99% or be demanded on every open; field reports of 20 MB to 1.6 GB after pasting a corridor and >100,000 RegApps.

complaints.theme: Autosave and backup have fine print that defeats them
complaints.detail: The autosave timer resets on every manual save so frequent savers may never get an .sv$; autosave stays off if a LISP routine or the Block Editor crashes mid-command; only one .bak generation is kept and none is written when saving to Forma Data Management since 2022.1; the Recovery Manager ignores never-saved drawings; full-time CRC validation is off by default because it slows opening.

eTransmit omits SHX/TTF fonts, .pat, .lin, .pmp, OLE links and URL references by default and can silently drop files; Bind renames every named object to name$0$name while Insert silently lets the local definition override the bound one; bind defects (parcel labels to '???', missing profile band labels) persisted across releases.

complaints.theme: File locking is delegated to the OS and goes stale
complaints.detail: Since AutoCAD 2000 the program does not control locking; .dwl/.dwl2 exist only for WHOHAS, survive crashes and cause 'in use or read-only' until deleted by hand; cloud drives 'often do not have any type of file locking'.

complaints.theme: Fault isolation is done by the user
complaints.detail: Standard remedies for fatal errors are: install updates, reset the user profile, update the GPU driver, uninstall plug-ins, purge/audit/recover, WBLOCK, clean reinstall; many crash classes are add-in, object-enabler or .NET/VC++ runtime interactions rather than core geometry.

Civil 3D at USD 2,870/yr list with no perpetual option; Vectorworks and SketchUp also subscription-only; Autodesk the company scores 1.5/5 on Trustpilot over auto-renewal billing; Flex tokens burn on idle sessions; network licences retired.

Blender ran at a loss in 2024 with reserves below target despite record income; the VC-backed FreeCAD company Ondsel shut down in Dec 2024 after its hosted SaaS failed to reach sustainable revenue (unverified, from memory).

BricsCAD, Bentley, Vectorworks and Carlson crash threads, G2/Capterra review text, BLS buyer counts and most open-source funding pages could not be opened (search budget exhausted after 12 queries; fetches proxy-blocked); those items are flagged unverified in the notes.

wishes: Business: free, perpetual, open desktop app; monetise a paid hosted project container + link-health service only after the desktop tool is in daily use (Ondsel lesson); paid support/training for firms and municipalities; sponsorship from survey-hardware, workstation and GPU vendors plus a small-donor programme (Blender model); later a plug-in marketplace; never dual licensing or core feature paywalls.

Stability: keep CADCraft's no-panic/catch_unwind/hostile-test discipline and add a CI gate on every PR; atomic saves with N-generation backups and a continuous change journal instead of a resettable 10-minute timer; autosave on web; per-object integrity hashes always on.
Stability: sandbox plug-ins (separate process or WASM) so add-ins, enablers and runtimes cannot take the host down; opt-in crash telemetry that files a reproducible report with the drawing excerpt.

Files: no RegApp/NOD-style bloat by construction, deterministic save, per-table size report; documented versioned object schema with forward and backward readers so 'save to older version' exists from day one.

Referencing: references by content identity plus project-relative path recorded in a project manifest (xrefs, data links, images, fonts, templates, plot styles with hash/size/mtime/role); relocation, packaging (fonts, patterns, linetypes included) and eTransmit become a manifest copy.

Referencing: a linkcheck command reporting found/missing/refused/changed-since-load for every nested link, a file watcher raising 'reload available', persisted reference state (Unloaded, found-at), colour-coded link health in the palette.

Collaboration: shared design objects referenced by ID through the manifest rather than per-user XML path files; explicit lock/merge semantics; local-first sync that never discards local work (keep both versions on conflict).

Containment: one movable project folder; copy = deep copy with link rewrite; paste/insert/bind merge rules (existing name wins, anonymous names regenerated) shown in a preview so nothing changes silently.
